entries.subject: Celestia native nucleus illustration and catalog scale
entries.finding: Superseded 2026-09-16: the Celestia generic mesh was a shared illustration with no relation to this nucleus, and its catalogue radius was an estimate. The package now shows a smooth ellipsoid at the published effective radius (Szabó et al. (2012), ApJ 761, 8); no mesh from Celestia is retained.
entries.revisitWhen: A measured shape model of this nucleus (radar, spacecraft or a convex lightcurve inversion with a stated pole) would replace the ellipsoid.

entries.subject: Published event and observation context
entries.finding: Retained intake decision: Hale–Bopp remained visible to the naked eye for about 18 months in 1996 and 1997. Its unusually large nucleus helped make it one of the most memorable comets of the twentieth century. The cited material supplies explanatory context; it does not qualify photographic terrain on this nucleus.

entries.subject: Published effective nucleus radius
entries.finding: Szabó et al. (2012), ApJ 761, 8: effective radius 37 km. A sphere; Fernández (2002) gives 30 ± 10 km by another method. The 11.35 hour period is not displayed. Used as the volume-equivalent radius of the displayed ellipsoid.
